text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.

- The U.N. Security Council expected to adopt Croatian government's letter of intent with no changes being made to it. Reliable sources also claim the State Department has made a positive assessment of the letter.

- Following a lengthy period without attacks, Bosnian Serbs on Monday night sprayed Slavonski Brod with automatic weapons fire. Some thirty shots were fired towards the center of town, but no one was hurt in the incident.
- The U.N. transitional administrator, general Jacques Klein says in an interview that he has devised a plan that will stop incidents during Eastern Slavonia elections.

- The telecommunications council announced on Monday that two radio frequencies are to be awarded to the city of Zagreb with bids coming in from three radio stations: Radio 101, Zagrebacki radio "Plavi 9" (running for both frequencies) and Zagrebacki krugoval.

- Three Croatian future motorways: Zagreb-Gorican, Zagreb-Macelj and Zagreb-Lipovac awaiting foreign investors with the BOT (Build, Operate, Transfer) model being the mode of financing Croatia would like to see.

- The Association of Serb Organizations at its Monday meeting described the Croatian government's letter of intent as acceptable, but stressed that the Serb side worked closely with the Croatian side on the document, but that fact is often being overlooked by the media. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
